purpose: Four DOJ Immigrant and Employee Rights Section telephone-intervention summaries represented as bounded case-level sequences from employment-document barriers through agency contact to reported job restoration or back pay.

events.date_precision: IER telephone-intervention summary date; page retrieved September 18, 2026
events.denominator: One reported worker case; no population denominator
events.method: Structured extraction from the official DOJ Civil Rights Division IER telephone-interventions page
events.missingness: Worker identity, employer identity, exact wage loss, payment instrument, receipt, accepted reemployment, household outcome, trust, action, and exit are not reported
events.exposure: An authorized worker had an automatically extended employment document that the employer rejected, resulting in lost work before IER intervention
events.alternatives_before_action: Other work, non-use, appeal routes, and the worker's feasible alternatives are not reported
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: The public summary reports six days of missed work and six days of back pay after the employer rehired the worker; net household effect is unknown
events.choice_or_response: The worker contacted IER and IER contacted the company's attorney; the worker's effort, timing, and acceptance of reemployment are not independently documented
events.person_or_actor_with_control: Employer controlled hiring and work access; IER controlled the intervention route; the worker's downstream control is not observed
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: Employer reportedly rehired the worker and paid six days of back pay after IER explained the document extension
events.remedy_receipt: Agency intervention summary reports rehire and back pay; independent worker confirmation is not retained
events.durability_followup: Later employment, recurrence, trust, and household recovery are unknown
events.immediate_outcome: Agency-reported job restoration and short-period wage remedy
events.protected_outcome: Continued employment and six days of reported back pay are described; worker-confirmed receipt and durable job security are not observed
events.sacrificed_outcome: Six days of work continuity and associated time or income were reportedly lost before intervention; broader opportunity and household costs remain unknown
events.cost_risk_transfer: The employer bears the reported back-pay response while the worker retains unknown transition, adequacy, and recurrence risk
events.later_outcome: No later employment, recurrence, household recovery, trust, collective action, switching, or exit endpoint is reported
events.meaning_and_attribution: No worker-reported fairness, blame, identity, or institutional-trust judgment is retained
events.public_or_collective_response: IER intervention is reported; no worker organizing, public action, or later complaint is observed
events.counterexample: A reported rehire and back-pay response can coexist with unmeasured receipt, adequacy, or future documentary risk
events.source_and_uncertainty: Official DOJ IER telephone-interventions page, https://www.justice.gov/crt/telephone-interventions-3; agency-reported case summary with no claimant follow-up

events.date_precision: IER telephone-intervention summary date; page retrieved September 18, 2026
events.denominator: One reported worker case; no population denominator
events.method: Structured extraction from the official DOJ Civil Rights Division IER telephone-interventions page

events.choice_or_response: The worker's case reached IER; whether the worker accepted reinstatement, received payment, or returned to work is not reported
events.person_or_actor_with_control: Employer controlled termination and offer; IER controlled the intervention route; worker control after the offer is unobserved
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: Employer reportedly issued back pay and offered reinstatement after IER explained that the card should not be reverified
events.remedy_receipt: Agency intervention summary reports back pay; accepted reinstatement and independent receipt are not retained
events.durability_followup: Later employment, recurrence, trust, and household recovery are unknown
events.immediate_outcome: Agency-reported back pay and reinstatement offer
events.protected_outcome: The payment and offer could address lost wages and access to the job; receipt, acceptance, and durable restoration are not observed
events.sacrificed_outcome: Eight weeks of work were reportedly missed; household, career, and dignity effects are not measured
events.cost_risk_transfer: The employer bears the reported payment and offer while the worker bears unknown acceptance, adequacy, and reemployment risk
events.later_outcome: No accepted reinstatement, later employment, recurrence, household recovery, trust, collective action, switching, or exit is reported
events.meaning_and_attribution: No worker-reported fairness, blame, identity, or institutional-trust endpoint is retained
events.public_or_collective_response: IER intervention is reported; no later collective or political response is observed
events.counterexample: An offer of reinstatement is not equivalent to accepted restoration, and back pay is not equivalent to full household recovery
events.source_and_uncertainty: Official DOJ IER telephone-interventions page, https://www.justice.gov/crt/telephone-interventions-3; agency-reported summary with no claimant follow-up

arrows.to: worker hotline contact and IER intervention
arrows.evidence: Four dated IER summaries describe a worker employment barrier followed by worker or advocate contact and an IER explanation to the employer
arrows.counterexample: These are selected intervention summaries, not a prevalence sample or complete record of all affected workers
arrows.remaining_gap: Worker denominator, effort, alternatives, non-use, and counterfactual opportunity

arrows.to: employer correction, rehire, or continued-work decision
arrows.evidence: The summaries report employers accepting documents, allowing continued work, rehiring, or offering reinstatement after IER contact
arrows.counterexample: The public page reports the employer decision but does not independently verify worker acceptance or sustained implementation
arrows.remaining_gap: Worker confirmation, start/return date, work conditions, and later recurrence

arrows.evidence: The page reports six days of back pay, $3,400, $264, and $2,615 in the four selected summaries; the Miami case also reports a reinstatement offer
arrows.counterexample: Agency-reported payment is not an independently audited receipt, and a reinstatement offer is not accepted reemployment
arrows.remaining_gap: Payment instrument, date, net amount, receipt, acceptance, and adequacy

arrows.to: durable work, household recovery, trust, action, switching, or exit
arrows.evidence: The public intervention summaries stop at the employer decision and reported back pay or offer; no downstream worker-linked endpoint is reported
arrows.counterexample: A short-term correction can coexist with unresolved household loss, recurrence risk, or changed institutional trust
arrows.remaining_gap: Worker-linked receipt, accepted restoration, later employment, household recovery, meaning, recurrence, collective action, switching, and exit

boundary: This ledger formalizes four selected DOJ IER telephone-intervention summaries. It strengthens the observed or reported sequence from employment barrier through agency intervention to employer correction and reported back pay, but it does not establish prevalence, worker-confirmed receipt, durable employment, household recovery, trust, action, switching, or exit.
storage_boundary: No claimant files, direct identifiers, employer identities, bulk archive, or payment instruments are retained; only bounded public case summaries, dates, reported remedy fields, uncertainty, and open arrows are represented.
